merger_description:
Pursuant to an agreement and plan of merger, Kite Parent Holdings, LP, which is controlled by private equity funds managed and/or advised by Summit Partners, L.P. (**Summit Partners**), proposes to indirectly acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of KF Parent, Inc., which is the parent company of the Keyfactor group (**Keyfactor**) (the **Acquisition**).

On completion of the Acquisition, Keyfactor will be solely controlled by funds advised and/or managed by Summit Partners and/or its affiliates.

Summit Partners is an experienced private equity investor founded in 1984. Summit Partners and its affiliates seek to invest in companies in the technology, healthcare & life sciences and growth products and services sectors across North America, Europe and worldwide.

Keyfactor is a provider of IT security and digital trust solutions specialising in machine identity management. Machine identity management is a security framework designed to control access by non-human entities to digital resources. Keyfactor’s technology secures, tracks and governs non-human identities that authenticate using cryptographic credentials.

Keyfactor is currently majority owned and controlled by funds managed and/or advised by Insight Venture Management, LLC and/or its affiliates.

determination_table_content.details:
Kite Parent Holdings, LP, which is controlled by private equity funds
managed and/or advised by Summit Partners, L.P. (Summit
Partners), applied for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed
indirect acquisition of 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of
capital stock of KF Parent, Inc., which is the parent company of the
Keyfactor group (Keyfactor), pursuant to an agreement and plan of
merger, as described in the transaction documents provided as part
of the application (the Acquisition).
On completion of the Acquisition, Keyfactor will be solely controlled
by funds advised and/or managed by Summit Partners and/or its
affiliates.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Summit Partners, is an experienced private equity
investor founded in 1984. Summit Partners and its affiliates seek to
invest in companies focused in the technology, healthcare & life
sciences and growth products and services sectors across North
America, Europe and worldwide.
The target, Keyfactor, is a provider of IT security and digital trust
solutions specialising in machine identity management, primarily
Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Certificate Lifestyle Management
(CLM). Machine identity management is a security framework
designed to control access by non-human entities to digital
resources. Keyfactor’s technology secures, tracks and governs non-
human identities that authenticate using cryptographic credentials.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationships
between Summit Partners (or its connected entities) and
Keyfactor in the supply of IT security software (including PKI
and CLM software) in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of IT security software
(including PKI and CLM software) in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
